name: Amaarae
label: Interscope
lede: Amaarae grew up between the Bronx, Atlanta and Accra, kept getting told she didn't fit a genre, and made a Pitchfork top-ten album out of the mismatch.

eras.title: Accra, by way of Atlanta
eras.text: Ama Serwah Genfi grew up between New York, New Jersey, Atlanta and Accra, then landed in Ghana's alté scene, where nobody minded that her songs wouldn't sit in one genre.

years.src: Wikipedia: Amaarae · Alternative Press · The Guardian
years.h: Ama Serwah Genfi starts out in the Bronx
years.p: Her childhood splits between New York, New Jersey, Atlanta and Accra, including several years at Ghana International School.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives her birth as July 4, 1994, to Ama Bawuah and Kwadwo Boateng Genfi. Alternative Press says the moving around exposed her to different music subcultures, and that her stage name blends her own first name with Corinne Bailey Rae's.

She has named Kelis's video for "Young, Fresh n' New" as a teenage lightning bolt. She told The Guardian it showed her "all avenues are valid". She studied English literature at Agnes Scott College near Atlanta, graduated in June 2017 and went back to Ghana.

years.h: Passionfruit Summers goes out on her own label, Golden Child
years.p: She had moved home to Ghana only months before. She has since said she first called the sound "Afro-fusion".
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the EP as a 2017 release on Golden Child LLC, with "Fluid" as its notable track and a video. The Guardian reports she originally called the music Afro-fusion before becoming a figure in the alté scene.

Wikipedia adds that she had already made a mixtape, In Splendid Isolation, at 17 while still in Ghana.

years.h: The first Boiler Room in Accra books her, and she's still independent
years.p: March 23 puts Amaarae on the bill with La Meme Gang and Kwesi Arthur, two of the city's biggest names.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Accra Boiler Room to March 23, 2019 and lists her with La Meme Gang and Kwesi Arthur. That same year she appeared on Wande Coal's "Spend Some Time" and on features for Show Dem Camp and TEMS ("Too Bad") and Mina ("Platinum Sex").

eras.title: The angel and the TikTok money
eras.text: The debut album mapped her sound. Then one song with a Ghanaian friend and a Colombian-American star carried it around the world.

years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Amaarae · The Guardian
years.h: The Angel You Don't Know won't stay in one genre
years.p: Pitchfork put the debut at No. 19 on its albums of 2020, and reviewer Owen Myers credited her voice and "confidence in spades".
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the album as a Golden Child release and says Pitchfork labelled it Best New Music. Myers wrote that it blended "alté, R&B, Southern rap, mall-rock, and Top 40 pop", according to Album of the Year's summary of the review.

The Guardian quoted her saying the record "presents the black woman as a deity". Sources differ by a day on the release date (Nov 12 vs Nov 13), and the Guardian piece lists Platoon as the label at the time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sad Girlz Luv Money · Wikipedia: Amaarae
yt: Sad Girlz Luv Money Remix (lyric video)
years.h: Kali Uchis joins "Sad Girlz Luv Money" and it hits the Hot 100
years.p: The remix of the 2020 track she made with [[Moliy|3472754c-1a8f-4466-aad8-b42626bbe8b0]] peaked at No. 80 in the US, with a TikTok push behind it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls the original a track by Amaarae and Ghanaian artist [[Moliy|3472754c-1a8f-4466-aad8-b42626bbe8b0]] from The Angel You Don't Know, produced by Onaduja Reuben Yinka. The Kali Uchis version came out September 16, 2021, hit No. 26 on Billboard's Global 200 and No. 3 in Lithuania.

It went platinum in the US, Canada and New Zealand, and gold in France, Poland and Portugal, per Wikipedia's certification table.

eras.title: A major label, a fountain
eras.text: Interscope signed on, Amaarae kept her collaborators, and the album that followed got the best reviews of her career.

years.h: Kendrick Lamar's Ghana listening party has her on the list
years.p: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers gets played in Accra for Amaarae, Black Sherif, Stonebwoy and Smallgod.

years.h: Fountain Baby is her first record for Interscope
years.p: Thirty-nine minutes long. Pitchfork named it Best New Music and No. 7 of 2023; Metacritic scored it 95 from eight reviews.
years.xp:
Wikipedia counts four singles: "Reckless & Sweet", "Co-Star", "Wasted Eyes" and "Angels in Tibet". Alternative Press says it took three years after her debut and reunited her with [[Kyu Steed|29ffa537-3504-48f0-aa1e-0c17a13dc15b]] and KZ Didit.

She told Alt Press a fountain baby is "a blessed child of God" with endless charisma. Pitchfork's Julianne Escobedo Shepherd called it "one of the best pop albums of the year".

years.src: NPR: Amaarae Tiny Desk · Wikipedia: Amaarae
years.h: Amaarae is the first Ghanaian to play the Tiny Desk
years.p: An 11-piece band squeezes behind the desk for "Wasted Eyes", "Big Steppa" and "Sad Girlz Luv Money".
years.xp: NPR said the set showed how far West African sounds have stretched into the US and that her music "defies catch-all labels like 'Afrobeats'". Wikipedia credits her as the first Ghanaian to perform there.

years.cap: Fountain Baby Tour, House of Blues, Chicago, March 21, 2024
years.h: Roses Are Red, Tears Are Blue stretches Fountain Baby by seven songs
years.p: It arrives with a 6lack remix. She also guests on [[Childish Gambino|7fb57fba-a6ef-44c2-abab-2fa3bdee607e]]'s "In the Night", with Jorja Smith.

eras.title: Black Star
eras.text: She played Coachella, shaved her head on stage, and spent the summer on a Brazil-to-Accra dance record that Pitchfork ranked in its year's top ten.

years.big: "A lotta the music you just heard is from my home country."
q: I love my country so much.
years.h: Coachella's Gobi stage gets a Ghanaian solo act for the first time
years.p: She plays unreleased songs and Ghanaian tracks by La Meme Gang, Asakaa Boys and Joey B, shaves her head mid-set and announces Black Star.
years.xp:
The Independent and Yahoo News reported the 5 p.m. set on the Gobi stage and the head-shave. Wikipedia says she was the first Ghanaian to play Coachella as a solo act.

Her next line to the crowd: "I love my country so much."

years.src: PAPER · NPR: Black Star review · Wikipedia: Black Star
years.h: Baile funk, by way of Brazil
years.p: She told PAPER she went to Brazil to "honor the craft", then mixed baile funk with her Ghanaian influences.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits [[Kyu Steed|29ffa537-3504-48f0-aa1e-0c17a13dc15b]], as co-producer with Amaarae, and lists Ape Drums, El Guincho, Forthenight, [[WondaGurl|b432152b-ab35-40eb-916b-dc8d1559046b]] and others among the producers. The album also borrows from highlife, Jersey club, house and Eurodance, per NPR.

years.h: "S.M.O." arrives first, two months ahead of Black Star
years.p: Pitchfork later ranks it No. 3 among the year's best songs.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Star · Year-End Lists · NPR: Black Star review
years.h: Black Star finishes at No. 10 on Pitchfork's 2025 list
years.p: Pitchfork also gave it 8.8 and Best New Music; NME and Rolling Stone gave it five stars.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Metacritic at 83 from nine reviews, the Guardian at four of five, and a No. 17 peak on Billboard's World Albums chart. NPR said the album treats the dance floor as sanctuary and names guests including Bree Runway, PinkPantheress, Charlie Wilson and Naomi Campbell.

The score came from Wikipedia's reception box; the No. 10 rank from Year-End Lists' copy of Pitchfork's ranking.

years.h: "Fineshyt" gets its video on album day
